title: Brazil's Black Majority and the 34% Pay Gap at the Top | Across the Water, Ep. 15
lede: Black and brown Brazilians are 55.5% of the country, 112.7 million people, more than twice the Black population of the United States. They now outnumber white business owners. But in 2024, Black directors and managers earned 34% less than white ones, and in B3's 2026 study of 290 listed companies only 2% had a preto statutory director. Four days before Brazil's national Black Consciousness holiday, this episode explains the pay gap, the boardroom gap, the jobs gap and the ownership story.
keyPoints: Census 2022: 45.3% pardo and 10.2% preto; together 55.5% of Brazil, 112.7 million people (IBGE, via Alma Preta).

In 2024 Black directors and managers averaged R$6,446 a month vs R$9,831 for white ones, 34% less; across all workers, white workers earned 65.9% more (IBGE Síntese de Indicadores Sociais, via Agência Brasil).
B3 and Instituto Locomotiva, 290 listed companies, 2026: 18% have a pardo board member, 5% a preto one; 2% have a preto statutory director (B3, Aug 12, 2026).
Q2 2026 unemployment: white 4.2%, pardo 6.1%, preto 6.9%; national 5.4%, falling to 5.2% in Q3 (IBGE PNAD Contínua).
Sebrae counts more than 16 million Black business owners (up 28.3% in ten years) vs about 14 million white owners (Sebrae, PNAD Contínua 2024).
